name: Tor Browser
description: A hardened browser that routes web traffic through the Tor network to reduce tracking and hide your source IP.
protects: Routes the browser’s traffic through multiple Tor relays so websites do not receive your source IP address.
Reduces cross-site tracking and browser fingerprinting with a deliberately standardized browser configuration.
Clears browsing history by default and limits cookies to the current session.
limitations: Tor Browser protects only traffic inside the browser, not other apps on your device.
Signing in or sharing identifying information can reveal who you are to a service even when your IP is hidden.
Tor cannot guarantee perfect anonymity. Downloads, add-ons and torrenting can expose you or weaken its protections.
account: No account is required to download or use Tor Browser.

name: Signal
description: An end-to-end encrypted messenger for private messages, voice calls and video calls.
protects: End-to-end encrypts Signal-to-Signal messages and calls so their content is available only to participants.
Supports disappearing messages and safety-number verification for sensitive conversations.
Usernames and phone-number privacy settings can let you connect without showing your number to new contacts.
limitations: Both participants need Signal; it no longer sends or receives ordinary SMS or MMS.
A phone number that can receive a registration code is still required to create an account.
Encryption protects message content, but it cannot protect a compromised device or prevent a recipient from copying what you send.
account: A Signal account and a phone number able to receive a registration code are required. Desktop apps are linked to a registered account.

name: Proton Mail
description: An encrypted email service with zero-access storage and automatic end-to-end encryption between Proton users.
protects: Stores mailbox content with zero-access encryption so Proton does not hold the key needed to read it.
Automatically end-to-end encrypts messages exchanged between Proton Mail users.
Offers password-protected messages and PGP for end-to-end encrypted mail with people on other providers.
limitations: Mail sent to another provider uses transport encryption by default, not end-to-end encryption, unless you use PGP or a password-protected message.
Email addressing metadata and subject lines are not end-to-end encrypted.
An email service improves message confidentiality but does not make your identity or network activity anonymous.
account: A Proton account is required. A free plan is available; recovery options should be configured carefully.

name: Mullvad VPN
description: A paid VPN that encrypts traffic to its servers and replaces your public IP with a shared address.
protects: Encrypts network traffic between your device and the selected Mullvad VPN server.
Replaces your public IP address with one shared by other customers, reducing direct IP-based linking by destinations.
Includes leak protection and a kill switch in its apps to reduce accidental traffic outside the VPN tunnel.
limitations: A VPN shifts trust from your internet provider to the VPN operator; it does not make you anonymous by itself.
Websites can still identify you through accounts, cookies, browser fingerprinting and information you disclose.
The service is paid, and an active subscription is required to connect.
account: Mullvad uses a randomly generated account number instead of an email/password login. The VPN requires paid time on that account.
